issues.legal_issue: The ordinary-residence condition for succession to a tenancy applies to heirs of a tenant remaining in possession after termination, not to heirs of a contractual tenant.
material_facts: The deceased held a contractual tenancy when she died.
The claimant was found to be the deceased tenant’s daughter and heir; that finding was not challenged.
The trial court had also found that the claimant was not ordinarily residing with the deceased, but the appellate court’s decision did not depend on that question.
issues.conclusion: The claimant inherited the contractual tenancy as the deceased tenant’s heir, irrespective of whether she was ordinarily residing with the deceased at the time of death; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(h) of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956, as amended in 1965, the words concerning the death of a person continuing in possession after termination refer to that person alone. The ordinary-residence condition therefore limits succession by heirs of a statutory tenant, not succession to a contractual tenancy, which is inheritable by the tenant’s heirs absent a provision to the contrary. The Court considered the Statement of Objects and Reasons as background to the amendment and relied on Anand Nivas (P) Ltd. v. Anandji Kalyanji Pedhi only to interpret Section 2(h), noting that its principle on inheritance of statutory tenancy had been overruled by Gian Devi Anand v. Jeevan Kumar.

predicates.tenancy_inheritance_dispute: A dispute over inheritance of a tenancy arose in an eviction proceeding.
predicates.deceased_had_subsisting_contractual_tena: The deceased tenant held a subsisting contractual tenancy when they died.
predicates.claimant_was_deceased_tenant_heir: The claimant was found to be an heir of the deceased tenant.

issues.definition: When an eviction dispute concerns inheritance of a tenancy, the deceased held a subsisting contractual tenancy, and the claimant was the deceased tenant’s heir, the claimant inherits the contractual tenancy.
